docs.title: Home
LightnerX
docs.text: LightnerX is a static C++17 library for building applications that communicate using the INER semantic protocol. The CMake project provides the LightnerX target; it neither produces nor requires its own executable. The library provides types for representing messages, interpreters, callbacks, connection management, and a transport layer based on GameNetworkingSockets.

docs.title: Why LightnerX?
docs.text: LightnerX keeps client-server communication simple through a clear message model and modular components:  Simple integration: connect networking and message handling through callbacks, while keeping control over initialization, update timing, and threads. Standardized communication: INER gives client and server a shared vocabulary for action requests, results, events, and informational updates, making each message's purpose and direction explicit. Modularity: compose message interpreters, connection management, and transport components according to your application's needs. Application flexibility: define your own message types and payloads while following the same communication model.  INER defines the meaning of messages exchanged between an Authority and an Obedient. It does not define sockets, connections, or an execution model. These capabilities are provided by LightnerX's networking components and can be connected to the application according to the developer's needs.  Build with CMake 3.22 or newer and a C++17 compiler. Public headers live under include/lightnerx/ ; byte views and results use the project’s own lightnerx::compact types. See Setup for dependencies and tested toolchains.

docs.title: Library, not a framework
docs.text: LightnerX provides reusable components. The consuming application decides:  when to initialize and shut down components; how to run update() ; which threads to use; how to organize the connection lifecycle; which components to use or replace with its own implementations.  For example, you can pass one complete INER message from your own transport to lightnerx::communication::MessageInterpreter . authorityInterpret does not require a connection. obedientInterpret requires a lightnerx::network::ConnectionManager registration: add() accepts only live GNS handles, so arbitrary identifiers from another transport are not supported by that path. The manager stores its own mapping and does not use GNS connection userdata.

docs.title: Key concepts
docs.text: Authority: controls internal states and receives intentions from the Obedient. Obedient: sends intentions to the Authority and receives events and responses. Event: an occurrence communicated by the Authority. Response: the result of an intention sent by the Obedient. Intention: an action request sent to the Authority. Notification: information sent to the Authority without requesting a state change.

docs.title: INER message flow
docs.text:
The INER protocol defines four message types exchanged between the Authority and the Obedient: Choose the message type according to its purpose and direction. In a typical client-server application, the server acts as the Authority and the client as the Obedient. Message type Direction When to use it Examples Intention Client → Server Request an action that the Authority must evaluate. Move a player, fire a weapon, use an item, join a match. Notification Client → Server Report information without requesting a change to the Authority's internal state. Report measured ping/latency, FPS, or client diagnostics. Event Server → Client Communicate an occurrence or state update from the Authority. A player joined, an entity moved, a projectile spawned, a match started. Response Server → Client Return the outcome of a specific Intention, linked by its correlationId . Movement approved, firing denied because ammunition is insufficient, an action partially applied, or processing failed. These examples describe application-defined messages; LightnerX does not provide built-in gameplay commands or telemetry formats. A Response reports an Intention's outcome, while an Event communicates an occurrence to the relevant clients. flowchart LR A["🖥️ AUTHORITY
Server"] O["💻 OBEDIENT
Client"] A -->|EVENT| O A -->|RESPONSE| O O -->|INTENTION| A O -->|NOTIFICATION| A classDef authority fill:#123456,stroke:#2699ff,color:#fff,stroke-width:2px classDef obedient fill:#302050,stroke:#a76bee,color:#fff,stroke-width:2px class A authority class O obedient linkStyle 0 stroke:#2596ee,stroke-width:3px linkStyle 1 stroke:#16a085,stroke-width:3px linkStyle 2 stroke:#e69b27,stroke-width:3px linkStyle 3 stroke:#a76bee,stroke-width:3px In LightnerX, the application connects components through callbacks: the network delivers bytes, and MessageInterpreter interprets those bytes according to the direction of communication. When sending, lightnerx::network::Target lets you select a connection, a group, or a broadcast with or without exceptions.

Runtime contracts
docs.text: One started Client or Server owns networking per process. Both classes have stable addresses and cannot be copied or moved. Server::close() and either owner's destructor release the runtime; a client can disconnect and reconnect without being destroyed. Direct networkInit() / networkKill() remain available when using the transport without a wrapper. See API reference for shutdown, callback exceptions, reentrancy and message validation contracts.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Setup ¶ LightnerX is a static C++17 library. CMake provides the LightnerX target. The application supplies its own executable. Dependencies and toolchain ¶ Use CMake 3.22 or newer , a C++17 compiler, and a build tool such as Ninja. CMake 3.22 is the minimum selected for compatibility with older development environments; CMake's version and the C++ language standard are independent requirements. Linux was validated with GCC 14.2 and Clang 19.1 in Debug and Release. GCC/libstdc++ 15.2 additionally validates the native comparison tests. Other platforms have not been validated by this migration. GameNetworkingSockets is pinned as a submodule in external/GameNetworkingSockets . Initialize it from the repository root: git submodule update --init --recursive Install OpenSSL and Protobuf development packages, the Protobuf compiler, and Python 3 when building tests. For example, on Debian 13: sudo apt-get install cmake g++-14 clang-19 ninja-build libssl-dev libprotobuf-dev protobuf-compiler python3-venv pkg-config
cmake --version Use a distribution package providing CMake 3.22 or newer. To reproduce the minimum-version check independently of the system package: python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install cmake==3.22.0
export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" If dependencies live in a separate prefix, pass -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/path/to/prefix when configuring. The local validation used Protobuf 3.21.12, OpenSSL 3.6.5 and Ninja 1.13.2. Build ¶ cmake -S . -B build/debug -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build/debug --parallel 2 To select a compiler, pass -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=gcc-14 -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=g++-14 , or -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-19 -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++-19 , in a fresh build directory. Use -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release for a release build. Consuming with CMake ¶ The target propagates C++17, LightnerX headers, GameNetworkingSockets headers, compile definitions and link requirements. Consumers link LightnerX : cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.22)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)
project(MyGame LANGUAGES C CXX)

add_subdirectory(external/LightnerX)
add_executable(game main.cpp)
target_link_libraries(game PRIVATE LightnerX) #include <lightnerx/network/client.hpp>

int main() {
    lightnerx::network::Client client;
    return client.start() ? 0 : 1;
} Use ordinary headers and sources with compatible compiler and standard-library ABIs. Each former module has a corresponding header, for example <lightnerx/network/server.hpp> , with definitions in network/server.cpp . The independent tests/consumer project checks propagated requirements and shared network/queue state across translation units. All public headers also compile in isolation. Byte views use lightnerx::compact::span , and results use lightnerx::compact::expected . These are LightnerX implementations of the C++20 std::span and C++23 std::expected contracts for C++17; see compact types for supported operations and language limitations. Regression tests ¶ cmake -S . -B build/tests -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DLIGHTNERX_BUILD_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build/tests --parallel 2
ctest --test-dir build/tests --output-on-failure Tests include deterministic protocol characterization, routing and allocation failures, the complete client ID domain, callbacks, ownership, multi-file consumers, and the compact types. They also compile the documentation's C++ examples. Assertions remain enabled in Release. Network integration requires local UDP socket access; a build alone does not validate network behavior. To compare the compact types against the native standard types, use GCC/libstdc++ 15.2 and enable the separate reference executables: cmake -S . -B build/native -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
  -DLIGHTNERX_BUILD_TESTS=ON -DLIGHTNERX_BUILD_NATIVE_REFERENCE_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build/native --parallel 2
ctest --test-dir build/native --output-on-failure Only these reference executables require C++20/23. LightnerX and the compact tests remain in C++17. A missing or incompatible native implementation fails the optional reference build; tests are not silently skipped. GCC 14's native expected implementation has an older conversion-to-boolean defect, so it is not the oracle for this comparison. For cross-version UDP tests, also pass -DLIGHTNERX_REFERENCE_BINARY=/absolute/path/to/original/lightnerx_test_lifecycle . CTest then pairs the old server with the new client and the new server with the old client. Migration validation identifies the original revision and build requirements. The CI workflow builds it separately. Sanitizers ¶ cmake -S . -B build/sanitizers -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
  -DLIGHTNERX_BUILD_TESTS=ON -DLIGHTNERX_SANITIZERS=address,undefined
cmake --build build/sanitizers --parallel 2
ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1:halt_on_error=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1 \
  ctest --test-dir build/sanitizers --output-on-failure This instruments LightnerX and its consumers, including tests. Dependencies are not rebuilt with sanitizer instrumentation. The pinned GameNetworkingSockets build disables RTTI, so GNS-linked targets disable only UBSan's vptr check. All other selected checks remain enabled, and independent compact and transport/allocation mock tests retain vptr checks as well. Fault-injection tests enable both ASan and UBSan when sanitizers are requested. Enabled sanitizer diagnostics fail tests immediately. LeakSanitizer may require execution outside a ptrace-restricted sandbox.

docs.title: First steps
First steps
docs.text: The examples use the C++17 types in lightnerx::compact for byte views and error results.  This guide shows the essential flow for setting up a server and a client. The examples use LightnerX components directly and leave the execution model to the application. The two programs illustrate separate consuming applications; the library remains a static library.

docs.title: Server
Client
Execution model
docs.text: The server.update() and client.update() methods are called by the application. They can run on the main thread, on a dedicated thread, or within the consuming project's existing execution loop.  The library does not require a specific number of threads or a fixed interval between updates. Run these server and client examples in separate processes: exactly one started wrapper owns networking in each process. Wrappers cannot be copied or moved.  Receive callbacks run during update() , and interpretation callbacks run on the thread that calls the interpreter. When sharing components across threads, handle synchronization in the application. For the batcher, serialize initialization, queuing, clearing and flush calls, which operate on the same queue. Callback exceptions propagate after resource cleanup; catch them around update() if the application intends to continue. See callback behavior for supported reentrant operations.

docs.title: Batch sending
Next steps
docs.text: See Communication and the INER protocol to understand headers, destinations, and sending flows. See API reference for networking components, messages, Target , and the batcher.

docs.title: Communication and INER
Communication and the INER protocol
docs.text: The examples use the C++17 types in lightnerx::compact for byte views and error results.

docs.title: INER and LightnerX
docs.text: INER is a semantic protocol. It defines the meaning and organization of messages, but does not define sockets, addressing, threads, or the transmission mechanism.  LightnerX implements the protocol's message types and provides networking components based on GameNetworkingSockets. The division is:  Responsibility INER LightnerX Meaning of Event, Response, Intention, and Notification Yes Represented by C++ types Message identification Yes MBT::type , correlationId , and status fields Header encoding Yes Packed structures and converters Sockets and connections No Server , Client , and GameNetworkingSockets Execution model No Chosen by the application

docs.title: Authority
docs.text: The Authority controls internal states. It receives Intention and Notification from the Obedient and sends Event and Response .  In LightnerX, the server typically interprets received messages with:  interpreter.obedientInterpret(bytes, registry, connection, connections);

docs.title: Obedient
docs.text: The Obedient sends intentions to the Authority and receives information about occurrences and results.  In LightnerX, the client typically interprets received messages with:  interpreter.authorityInterpret(bytes);

docs.title: Message types
docs.text: Choose the message type according to its purpose and direction. In a typical client-server application, the server acts as the Authority and the client as the Obedient.  Message type Direction When to use it Examples Intention Client → Server Request an action that the Authority must evaluate. Move a player, fire a weapon, use an item, join a match. Notification Client → Server Report information without requesting a change to the Authority's internal state. Report measured ping/latency, FPS, or client diagnostics. Event Server → Client Communicate an occurrence or state update from the Authority. A player joined, an entity moved, a projectile spawned, a match started. Response Server → Client Return the outcome of a specific Intention, linked by its correlationId . Movement approved, firing denied because ammunition is insufficient, an action partially applied, or processing failed.  These examples describe application-defined messages; LightnerX does not provide built-in gameplay commands or telemetry formats. A Response reports an Intention's outcome, while an Event communicates an occurrence to the relevant clients.

docs.title: Event
docs.text: Event communicates an occurrence from the Authority. Its header contains:  BaseProtocol::size ; MBT::type , used as type_id .  The payload, when present, follows the header.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: Response relates the result to an intention through correlationId and contains a status .  The statuses are exposed by constants in the <lightnerx/communication/response.hpp> header:  Constant Value Meaning Type used by LightnerX APPROVED_RESPONSE 0 intention fully approved Response DENIED_RESPONSE 1 intention denied UnsuccessfulResponse PARTIALLY_APPROVED_RESPONSE 2 intention partially applied UnsuccessfulResponse FAILURE_RESPONSE 3 internal error during processing Response  A failure does not necessarily mean that the intention was denied; the application may decide to try again. UnsuccessfulResponse adds reasonCode to the header of denied or partially approved responses. For partial approval, the meaning of the payload is defined by the application.

docs.title: Intention
docs.text: Intention requests that the Authority perform an action. Its header contains:  BaseProtocol::size ; MBT::type ; correlationId .  The intention's payload follows this header.

docs.title: Notification
Binary representation
docs.text: Header structures are packed without additional padding using #pragma pack(push, 1) . The converters copy fields in the machine's native representation; participants must use a compatible representation for these fields and agree on the payload format.

docs.title: Messages from the Authority
docs.text:
The first field uses a combined value: the least significant bit indicates whether the message is a Response , and the remaining fifteen bits represent the size.  The table describes the recommended formats for emission: approved, denied and failure responses have no payload; partial approval may carry application-defined bytes.  Message Header Recommended content when sending Event 2 bytes of combined size + 2 bytes of type variable payload Response 2 bytes of combined size + 2 bytes of correlationId + 1 byte of status no payload for the statuses represented by Response UnsuccessfulResponse Response structure + 2 bytes of reasonCode variable payload for a partial response  When constructing the header, the combined value takes the form:  Event:    (total_size << 1) | 0
Response: (total_size << 1) | 1  The interpreter retrieves the size with base >> 1 and distinguishes Event from Response with base & 1 . In the headers delivered to the callback, protocol.size already contains the decoded size, without the type bit.  Reception currently tolerates additional bytes in responses when the declared total matches the supplied span and the selected header is complete. For approved and failure responses, the interpreter ignores those bytes and delivers an empty payload. For denied and partially approved responses, it delivers all bytes after UnsuccessfulResponse , even though the recommended denied-response format has no payload. protocol.size still includes the complete received message, including any ignored bytes; it can therefore exceed the header size plus the delivered payload size. This reception behavior does not change the recommended emission formats. Converters copy the supplied payload without enforcing status-specific payload rules.

docs.title: Messages from the Obedient
docs.text: In messages from the Obedient, size directly represents the total message size.  Message Header Content Notification 2 bytes of size + 2 bytes of type variable payload Intention 2 bytes of size + 2 bytes of type + 2 bytes of correlationId variable payload  The specified size must include the header and payload. Each interpretation call must receive exactly one complete message: the decoded total must equal the supplied span and the header must be complete, otherwise no callback is delivered. Authority messages are limited to 32767 bytes and Obedient messages to 65535 bytes. The interpreter does not split concatenated messages or buffer partial frames. Unknown response statuses are ignored. The converters copy the header and payload into a SteamNetworkingMessage_t ; they do not automatically construct the semantic value of the size field. They throw std::bad_alloc if GNS allocation fails and std::length_error if the allocation size cannot be represented.

docs.title: Identifiers
docs.text: type_id identifies the semantic type defined by the application and appears in the code as MBT::type . correlationId relates a response to its corresponding intention. The ID received in the server's interpreted message callback is the internal identifier assigned by ConnectionManager .  This internal ID belongs to the connection management implementation and is not an INER protocol field. The name originId does not designate a protocol field either. Network destinations use HSteamNetConnection handles, which are distinct from internal IDs and semantic identifiers.

docs.title: Network destinations
docs.text: lightnerx::network::Target , declared in the <lightnerx/network/target.hpp> header, defines where a queued message will be sent. The static factories create the destination description:  Factory Destination Target::single(connection) a specific connection Target::group(connections) all connections in the provided vector Target::broadcast() all connections registered in ConnectionManager Target::broadcast(exceptions) all connections registered in ConnectionManager , except the specified handles  Target::group stores the explicit selection of handles. Broadcast queries the ConnectionManager passed to flushAll at flush time, using the mappings maintained by the application. Its exceptions are also HSteamNetConnection handles.

docs.title: Receiving flow
docs.text:
Network -> Server callback -> obedientInterpret -> application callback
Network -> Client callback -> authorityInterpret -> application callback  MessageInterpreter delivers a lightnerx::communication::Message whose header contains the concrete type in a std::variant and whose payload is a lightnerx::compact::span<const std::byte> .  Callbacks run during the interpretation call. The header is delivered by value, but the span only references the received bytes. In the flow with Server or Client , these bytes are released after the receive callbacks. To retain the payload, copy its bytes during the callback; copying only Message keeps a reference to the same buffer.

docs.title: Sending flow
What each step does
docs.text: queueMessage receives the OutboundMessage from the converter and stores the same message with its destination, without allocating another message or copying the bytes. The call consumes the message: on success, the batcher keeps it until the flush; if the queue is full, it releases it immediately. The caller must not call Release() or reuse the message after passing it to the queue. A null pointer is rejected with invalid_argument .  flushAll iterates over pending messages, routes each one according to its destination, and releases the message received from the converter with Release() . All entries are processed and the queue is emptied even when send errors occur. The return value indicates success or the last error encountered among these operations.  Batching lets you accumulate multiple messages before a flush. Each entry remains a separate message; payloads are not concatenated. The application decides when to flush, for example at the end of an update. Success indicates that the transport accepted the send operations, without confirming processing by the recipient.  For Event and Response , the size field must use the combined value described above. For Intention and Notification , it uses the total size directly.  Pending batches can be discarded explicitly with clearMessagesBatcher() and are also released at actual network shutdown. A thrown send exception releases the complete queue before propagating to the caller.

docs.title: API reference
API reference
docs.text: This page groups public components by header. Include the indicated header with #include ; declarations belong to the indicated namespaces. Signature blocks are excerpts from class or namespace declarations, while usage blocks assume the objects described in their surrounding text.  The library uses its own C++17 compact types : lightnerx::compact::span provides a non-owning view of contiguous elements, and lightnerx::compact::expected holds a value or an error.  Operations that return lightnerx::compact::expected<void, std::error_code> can be checked with if (!result) . In the event of an error, result.error() provides the code and result.error().message() provides its description. Complete examples are available in First steps .

lightnerx::communication::MessageInterpreter
docs.text: Interprets received bytes and calls registered callbacks in registration order, during the interpretation call itself. More than one callback can be registered. Lambdas that capture objects by reference require those objects to remain alive while the callbacks run.

docs.title: Callback registration
Interpretation on the server
Interpretation on the client
docs.text: void authorityInterpret(lightnerx::compact::span<const std::byte> data);  Interprets Event and responses sent by the Authority. The type bit selects event or response; the status selects Response or UnsuccessfulResponse . The approved and failure statuses deliver an empty payload; denial and partial approval deliver the bytes following UnsuccessfulResponse .  This reception behavior is more permissive than the recommended emission formats. If the total size matches the supplied span and the header is complete, additional bytes in approved and failure responses are accepted but ignored; additional bytes in denied responses are delivered. The decoded protocol.size includes any ignored bytes, so it does not necessarily equal the header size plus the delivered payload size. See binary representation for both emission and reception rules.

lightnerx::compact::expected<void, std::error_code> sendToConnection(
    lightnerx::compact::span<const std::byte> message,

docs.title: Sending to a group
docs.text:
lightnerx::compact::expected<void, std::error_code> sendToConnections(
    lightnerx::compact::span<const std::byte> message,
    const std::vector<HSteamNetConnection> connections
);  Forwards the same bytes to each handle in the vector. Attempts all destinations and returns the first error encountered, if any.

docs.title: Broadcast
lightnerx::network::Target
lightnerx::network::OutboundMessage
Batcher
Validation and callback behavior
docs.text: Both interpretation methods accept exactly one complete message. The declared total size must equal the supplied span and include the entire header. Authority sizes are decoded from 15 bits (maximum 32767 bytes); Obedient sizes use 16 bits (maximum 65535 bytes). Truncated headers, mismatched sizes, unknown response status and unregistered Obedient origins produce no callback, matching the existing void parser interface. There is no incremental or concatenated-message framing.  Callbacks run synchronously. Registration during a callback is safe; newly registered callbacks participate from the next dispatch, including a nested interpretation. Existing callback objects retain mutable state. Receive/interpreter/ forEach exceptions propagate to their caller, with received buffers released even when a client batch is interrupted. Exceptions from GNS status callbacks are caught at the boundary and the first exception is rethrown by Server::update() after RunCallbacks() returns. A throwing callback ends its current callback sequence.  Recursive update() returns operation_in_progress . Callbacks may disconnect or request Server::close() ; do not destroy or assign the component executing a callback. Referenced objects must remain alive until dispatch finishes. A negative receive result returns io_error , distinct from an empty queue; the client also clears and closes its failed connection. Updating an unstarted/closed wrapper returns not_connected .  ConnectionManager owns an independent, bidirectional mapping; it neither reads nor writes GNS userdata. A handle may be registered once per manager. Adding a duplicate, invalid handle, or a handle beyond capacity returns nullopt . Different managers may independently register the same valid handle. getClientId() returns nullopt for an absent registration, including handle zero, and retains a registered identity after transport closure until removal. IDs range from 1 to 65535 and are recycled; negative capacities throw invalid_argument , capacity above 65535 is capped. forEach visits the index range present on entry, safely allowing add/remove; it may observe replacements within that range but does not extend traversal for vector growth.  The batch queue is global. initMessagesBatcher() reserves capacity without discarding queued messages. clearMessagesBatcher() releases pending messages and preserves capacity; actual network shutdown and queue destruction also release pending messages. flushAll() releases every queued message if a send throws, then propagates the exception; with returned error codes it attempts all entries and returns the last error. Serialize all batch operations, including clearing and shutdown.

docs.title: C++17 compact types
C++17 compact types
docs.text: LightnerX provides its own lightnerx::compact::span and lightnerx::compact::expected in ordinary, self-contained headers. They are implementations, not aliases for std::span (C++20) or std::expected (C++23). They do not add declarations to std , allocate internal storage, or depend on a newer language mode. Contained values and errors may themselves allocate.

docs.title: Byte views with span
Results with expected
C++17 limits and verification
docs.text: Span's scalar construction, observers and subviews are constexpr where C++17 allows them; byte reinterpretation is not a constant expression. Expected supports constexpr scalar in-place/value/error construction, simple observers and trivial copies. C++17 does not permit the placement construction/destruction needed to change union alternatives during constant evaluation, and its std::invoke is not constexpr. Consequently, expected's nontrivial/converting construction, state-changing operations and monadic calls are runtime operations in this implementation. Runtime behavior and exception guarantees remain covered by tests.  The same test sources run against compact in C++17 and native span/expected in C++20/23. The suite compares deterministic outputs, reference categories, constraints, extents, slices, byte views, move-only types, cv-void results, conversions, exception rollback, object lifetimes and monadic results. Invalid programs must fail compilation after a positive control succeeds. See Setup to run the comparisons. This is regression evidence for the tested contracts, not a claim that finite tests prove every possible instantiation equivalent.

docs.title: Migration and validation
docs.text: C++17 migration and validation ¶ The migration starts from 541ae1d39225ec9b747b9f888f96242a710e9073 , with GameNetworkingSockets pinned at d534c19aa760df3fb75fd20db13ba1932b8a5463 . The original repository's 38 text files, including 14 module units and six Markdown documents, were reviewed before implementation. The dependency's public interfaces and build requirements were checked without changing its source. Architecture and migration sequence ¶ The communication layer contains packed INER headers, notification registration, serialization and parsing. The network layer owns GNS initialization, client/server lifecycle, connection IDs, routing and a shared outbound queue. Applications connect the layers through synchronous callbacks and supply their own update loop. Implementation proceeded through independent commits: capture original behavior, add and test compact span, add and test compact expected, replace modules with headers/sources, switch the library and consumers to C++17, extend regressions and CI, then update and compile the documentation. All 14 module units now have declarations in include/lightnerx/{communication,network}/*.hpp and definitions in the corresponding .cpp files. Templates remain in headers. Network ownership and the outbound queue each retain one state shared across translation units. Public constants use inline variables so their addresses also remain shared. Public headers compile independently and tolerate repeated inclusion. Consumer source changes are limited to including the corresponding headers, using lightnerx::compact::span and lightnerx::compact::expected with their associated helpers, and selecting the new CMake configuration. The custom types implement the C++20 std::span and C++23 std::expected interfaces within the documented C++17 limits . Application names, callback shapes, ownership, error codes and protocol behavior remain the same. Consumers must be rebuilt; binary ABI compatibility with module builds or native standard-library types is not promised. CMake 3.22 or newer and the public cxx_std_17 requirement replace the experimental module build. Standard includes, iterator algorithms and explicit function templates replace newer language/library facilities. Setup contains current commands. Preserved behavior ¶ Packed header sizes remain Event 4, Notification 4, Intention 6, Response 5 and UnsuccessfulResponse 7 bytes. Native-endian fields and authority size/type encoding remain unchanged. Parsing still requires one complete frame, rejects truncation and unknown statuses, and preserves the existing extra-byte handling for approved, failure, denied and partially approved responses. Group and broadcast sends attempt every selected destination and return the first error. Queue flush attempts all entries, releases messages and returns the last error. Queuing consumes ownership even when rejected. Client and Server remain noncopyable and nonmovable, with one active network owner per process. Callback registration, exceptions, recursive-update rejection and deferred server close retain their behavior. Connection IDs remain 1–65535 with independent mappings, recycling, strong copy assignment and bounded mutation during iteration. Recorded baseline and differential tests ¶ The original C++26 revision was built separately with GCC/libstdc++ 15.2.0, CMake 4.2.3, Ninja 1.13.2, Protobuf 3.21.12 and OpenSSL 3.6.5. Its nine original tests passed without skips. CMake 4.2.3 is required only to reproduce that revision's experimental standard-library module configuration. Fixture provenance records the platform, revision and toolchain. The captured fixture includes error codes, serialized bytes and a deterministic parsing corpus with seed 0x4c58 : 13,275 invocations, 1,897 delivered messages and digest 14252850176607638377 . The C++17 executable must reproduce the entire output byte for byte. Runtime handles, addresses, ephemeral ports, timings and localized error strings are excluded. The fixture was recorded on Linux x86_64 with little-endian fields; it is not a claim of cross-endian wire compatibility. The compact tests run the same sources against native types in separate C++20/23 executables and compare outputs. Compile-time checks and invalid-program tests cover construction constraints and API contracts. Real UDP tests also pair the original server with the new client and the original client with the new server. The minimum was subsequently lowered to CMake 3.22 for compatibility. Header file sets (introduced in CMake 3.23) were replaced with ordinary private header source entries; include paths and C++17 requirements still propagate through the target. The original C++26 reference build retains its separate CMake 4.2.3 requirement. Local results ¶ Validation ran on Linux with CMake 4.5.0, GCC 14.2, Clang 19.1 and, for native comparisons, GCC/libstdc++ 15.2. The builds use C++17 except for the explicit native oracle targets and the separately built original revision. Configuration Result GCC 14 Debug 15/15 passed Clang 19 Debug 15/15 passed GCC 14 Release 15/15 passed Clang 19 Release 15/15 passed GCC 14 ASan, UBSan and leak detection 15/15 passed GCC 15 native comparisons and both cross-version UDP directions 22/22 passed All 56 C++ documentation blocks are compiled with C++17: complete examples retain their own includes, fragments receive explicit application contexts, and API excerpts are checked against the real declarations. The two compact examples also execute; the open-ended network example loops are compiled and linked only. Shell snippets pass syntax checking, and local document links are checked. These results include no skipped tests. Build directories retain results.xml , tests.log and CTest's Testing/Temporary/LastTest.log ; generated logs are not committed. The CI workflow repeats Linux compiler/configuration checks and the separate native/original-reference comparison, and uploads test artifacts. GameNetworkingSockets is not sanitizer-instrumented and disables RTTI. GNS-linked targets therefore exclude only UBSan's vptr check. The independent compact and mock tests retain all selected checks. Windows and macOS were not validated. See sanitizer instructions and compact limitations when interpreting coverage. Minimum CMake compatibility check ¶ The compatibility adjustment was validated with CMake/CTest 3.22.0 in fresh Linux Debug build directories. GCC 14 passed all 15 standard tests, including the independent consumer build and compiled documentation. GCC/libstdc++ 15 passed all 22 tests with native comparisons and both C++26/C++17 UDP directions enabled. Neither run skipped tests. Logs are in build/cmake322-gcc/ and build/cmake322-native/ . The CI compiler/configuration matrix now uses CMake 3.22.0 for the migrated project.

docs.title: Audit fixes
docs.text:
Correções da auditoria LightnerX — registro histórico ¶ Este documento preserva os resultados da auditoria de 12/11/2026, anterior à migração. O LightnerX atual usa C++17 e headers clássicos; a validação atual está em Migração C++17 e as instruções de build em Setup . Os caminhos da tabela abaixo foram atualizados para os arquivos atuais; os headers correspondentes estão em include/lightnerx/ . Números, logs e limitações descritos como históricos referem-se exclusivamente à auditoria. Revisão de origem: 8e5a352 . Dependência GNS: d534c19 . Auditoria lida: LightnerX-audit.md . Trabalho validado em 12/11/2026 com GCC/libstdc++ 15.2,
CMake 4.2.3 e Ninja 1.13.2, em Linux. Os 14 itens foram confrontados com a revisão de origem e receberam correções.
Naquela auditoria, C++26, módulos, GameNetworkingSockets, representação binária INER e queueMessage(OutboundMessage) com Target foram preservados. Não houve edição
de terceiros; a alteração preexistente em external/GameNetworkingSockets/examples/trivial_signaling_client.h foi mantida naquela auditoria. Resultado por item ¶ Os nomes de testes abaixo são os sufixos dos testes CTest lightnerx.* .
Os caminhos de implementação sem prefixo estão em network/ . LX Causa Correção implementada Arquivos de implementação/documentação Testes executados Classificação Pendências LX-01 Wrappers destruíam GNS diretamente, deixando flag e ponteiros inconsistentes. Encerramento central, ownership explícito, limpeza de membros e rollback de inicialização. network_manager.cpp , client.cpp , server.cpp , docs/api.md lifecycle , lifecycle_faults , integration Corrigido e validado Nenhuma funcional. LX-02 Consulta de identidade dependia de userdata em handle já fechado. Mapa reverso local mantém a identidade até remove() , inclusive nos callbacks após o fechamento. connection_manager.cpp , server.cpp , docs/api.md connection_manager , integration com desconexões pelos dois lados Corrigido e validado Nenhuma. LX-03 return false construía optional<uint16_t> presente com valor zero. Lookup ausente retorna nullopt ; zero não é um ID cadastrado. connection_manager.cpp connection_manager , messages Corrigido e validado Nenhuma. LX-04 Último ID não era reciclado; contador e índice de 16 bits transbordavam. Reciclagem de todos os IDs removidos, contador mais largo, domínio 1–65535 e iteração limitada com size_t . connection_manager.cpp , docs/api.md connection_manager : 70.000 ciclos; connection_manager_domain : domínio completo Corrigido e validado Domínio completo usa interface controlada, não 65.535 sockets reais simultâneos. LX-05 Cópia implícita duplicava ownership e ponteiros de callbacks. Cópia e movimentação excluídas em Client/Server; Server também encerra recursos no destrutor. client.cpp , server.cpp , docs/api.md lifecycle e consumer , com verificações de tipos em compilação Corrigido e validado Código consumidor que copiava wrappers deve ser adaptado. LX-06 Desconexão local não limpava handle e estado. Fechamento bem-sucedido invalida handle e limpa connected , permitindo reconexão. client.cpp , docs/api.md lifecycle_faults , integration Corrigido e validado Nenhuma. LX-07 Recebimento negativo era tratado como fila vazia. Retorna io_error ; cliente também fecha/limpa sua conexão inválida. client.cpp , server.cpp , docs/api.md lifecycle_faults , com retorno -1 nos dois caminhos Corrigido e validado Falha rara provocada por injeção controlada. LX-08 Cinco conversores desreferenciavam retorno nulo de AllocateMessage . Verificação comum lança bad_alloc ; tamanho irrepresentável lança length_error antes da alocação. communication/message.cpp , docs/api.md , docs/communication.md message_faults : cinco falhas de alocação e overflow; messages : GNS real Corrigido e validado Não foi necessário esgotar a memória do sistema. LX-09 C++26 e requisitos GNS não eram públicos no target; setup incompleto. cxx_std_26 e GNS públicos; configuração de import std e toolchain documentadas; consumidor independente. CMakeLists.txt , docs/setup.md , tests/consumer/ consumer , compilação completa CMake/Ninja Corrigido e validado Outras toolchains não foram homologadas. LX-10 Dois módulos exportavam constantes distintas com o mesmo nome. Uma declaração de k_invalidConnection no gerenciador global, reexportada por cliente e transporte. network_manager.cpp , client.cpp , transport.cpp consumer , lifecycle Corrigido e validado Nenhuma. LX-11 Instâncias competiam pelos callbacks e pela destruição global. Um wrapper iniciado por processo; conflitos e repetição de start são rejeitados; shutdown respeita o owner. network_manager.cpp , client.cpp , server.cpp , README.md , docs/api.md , docs/first-steps.md lifecycle , integration Corrigido e validado Coexistência de vários wrappers não faz parte do contrato suportado. LX-12 Userdata global permitia interferência entre managers e cadastros duplicados. Mapeamento bidirecional próprio, pertencimento local, rejeição de duplicatas e validação do handle GNS na admissão. connection_manager.cpp , README.md , docs/api.md connection_manager : duplicatas, managers independentes, userdata preservada Corrigido e validado Transporte externo não ganha suporte a IDs arbitrários; restrição documentada. LX-13 Parser ignorava divergência entre tamanho declarado e buffer. Exige uma mensagem completa, tamanho decodificado igual ao span e header mínimo completo. communication/message.cpp , docs/api.md , docs/communication.md messages , message_faults : truncamentos, concatenação, tamanhos inválidos e limites 15/16 bits Corrigido e validado Nenhuma mudança de framing ou formato binário. LX-14 Exceções vazavam buffers; registro reentrante invalidava vetores; forEach terminava o processo. RAII em recebimento e batching, callbacks em armazenamento estável, propagação de exceções, captura na fronteira GNS, bloqueio de update recursivo e fechamento adiado. client.cpp , server.cpp , connection_manager.cpp , network_manager.cpp , message_batch.cpp , communication/message.cpp , docs/api.md messages , message_faults , lifecycle_faults , connection_manager , integration ; ASan e UBSan conforme limites abaixo Corrigido, mas parcialmente validado UBSan modular indisponível no GCC 15.2; checagem vptr incompatível com GNS sem RTTI. Evidências e testes históricos ¶ A suíte normal passou nos oito testes, sem testes ignorados. Resultados locais: build/audit/test-results.xml e build/audit/Testing/Temporary/LastTest.log .
A execução instrumentada final também passou nos oito testes, sem testes
ignorados e sem diagnósticos dos sanitizadores habilitados (53,47 segundos).
Resultados: build/audit-sanitizers/test-results.xml e build/audit-sanitizers/Testing/Temporary/LastTest.log . A suíte normal levou
131,90 segundos, incluindo a compilação do consumidor. Os limites abaixo são
parte da validação, não uma garantia de ausência de todos os defeitos possíveis.
A classificação final é de 13 itens corrigidos e validados e LX-14 corrigido,
mas parcialmente validado pelas restrições de instrumentação explicitadas. Os executáveis connection_manager , messages e lifecycle importam os
  módulos reais e usam GNS real. Há testes de reinicialização, estados inválidos,
  identidade, serialização, ownership e callbacks. integration executa Client e Server em processos separados sobre UDP local.
  Testa três sessões, mensagens, reconexão, desconexão iniciada pelos dois lados,
  identidade após fechamento, exceção de admissão, registro reentrante de
  callbacks, update recursivo e encerramento/reinicialização do servidor. consumer configura um projeto pai independente, inclui headers Steam e
  importa módulos ligando somente o target LightnerX . Os três testes Python suplementares compilam corpos de produção sem as
  declarações de módulos. Interfaces controladas permitem esgotar os 65.535 IDs,
  devolver alocação nula e provocar erros de recebimento/liberação. Eles não
  substituem os testes dos módulos reais. Contadores verificam a liberação de
  mensagens, inclusive após uma parte do lote já ter sido processada. Reproduções anteriores às correções incluíram: Client copiável; três mensagens
retidas após exceção; desconexão com connected=true ; erro de recebimento
reportado como sucesso; inicialização global verdadeira com interface nula;
start simultâneo/repetido aceito; optional inválido com valor zero; duplicatas;
overflow de IDs; tamanho INER inválido entregue; alocação nula causando falha.
O consumidor original não encontrava o header Steam e compilava em C++17.
O teste de domínio também foi aplicado ao arquivo original de 8e5a352 e falhou
em exhausted ID domain must reject add ( build/audit/id-baseline.log ). Reprodução com a versão C++17 atual ¶ Os comandos abaixo executam a suíte atual; não recriam os oito testes históricos. Para reproduzir o ambiente antigo, use a revisão e a toolchain daquela auditoria. O problema UBSan/módulos descrito abaixo não se aplica mais à implementação C++17; somente a incompatibilidade de vptr com GNS sem RTTI permanece. cmake -S . -B build/audit -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DLIGHTNERX_BUILD_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build/audit --parallel 2
ctest --test-dir build/audit --output-on-failure --output-junit test-results.xml -j 2

cmake -S . -B build/audit-sanitizers -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DLIGHTNERX_BUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DLIGHTNERX_SANITIZERS=address,undefined
cmake --build build/audit-sanitizers --parallel 2
ctest --test-dir build/audit-sanitizers --output-on-failure --output-junit test-results.xml -j 2 O teste UDP e LeakSanitizer precisam de permissões que o sandbox inicial não
oferecia. A execução final usa o ambiente autorizado fora dessa restrição.
O limite dos testes que compilam código foi ampliado para 180 segundos após um
timeout de compilação concorrente; os limites de runtime permanecem delimitados. Limites históricos dos sanitizadores ¶ Os módulos LightnerX e os consumidores foram compilados com ASan. Os três testes
suplementares usam ASan e UBSan, com -fno-sanitize-recover=all , para que qualquer
diagnóstico habilitado resulte em falha. A biblioteca padrão e o GNS não foram
instrumentados nem tiveram seus fontes alterados. GCC 15.2 aborta com erro interno cp/module.cc:10037 ao compilar estes módulos
com UBSan. Isso foi reproduzido tanto instrumentando std quanto deixando std sem instrumentação; portanto não se declara cobertura UBSan dos módulos reais. O GNS vendorizado usa -fno-rtti . Uma reprodução independente, contendo apenas
Init/CreatePollGroup/DestroyPollGroup/Kill de GNS, já produz o diagnóstico vptr
do UBSan, sem usar LightnerX. O mesmo programa passa quando somente essa checagem
é desabilitada ( build/audit/gns-ubsan-probe.cpp e .log ). Por isso apenas o
teste suplementar de ciclo de vida, que chama a biblioteca real, usa -fno-sanitize=vptr . Os outros dois testes suplementares não precisam dessa
exclusão. Esse diagnóstico foi investigado mesmo quando CTest inicialmente
reportou sucesso por causa do modo recuperável padrão do UBSan. API pública e contratos preservados ¶ Client e Server não podem mais ser copiados ou movidos. Server ganha destrutor
  com limpeza automática; close() é idempotente e noexcept . Apenas um Client ou Server iniciado possui a rede por processo. Start repetido
  retorna operation_in_progress ; outro owner retorna device_or_resource_busy . networkKill() não invalida um wrapper ativo; o encerramento ocorre quando o
  owner libera os recursos. Raw GNS Kill/RunCallbacks durante esse ownership não
  são operações suportadas. disconnect() limpa o estado local imediatamente. Erros de recebimento passam
  a retornar io_error . Callbacks podem lançar; buffers são liberados e a
  exceção é propagada. Não se deve destruir o objeto que está despachando um
  callback. forEach deixa de ser incondicionalmente noexcept . getClientId() consulta pertencimento ao manager e não userdata GNS. A
  identidade persiste até remoção explícita. O manager deixa userdata para a
  aplicação. Capacidades negativas são rejeitadas; o domínio é limitado a 65535. Conversores mantêm assinaturas e lançam bad_alloc / length_error em falhas.
  Mensagens recebidas com tamanho inconsistente são rejeitadas sem callback,
  conforme a interface de parsing existente, que retorna void . Adicionados clearMessagesBatcher() e Target::isGroup() . A API queueMessage() /Target permanece; mensagens pendentes são liberadas no
  encerramento e após exceções. initMessagesBatcher() não descarta a fila. Há uma única constante pública k_invalidConnection . CMake agora propaga C++17 e
  os requisitos públicos GNS. O consumidor inclui os headers clássicos descritos em Setup . Não há decisão arquitetural pendente para as correções adotadas. As restrições
de múltiplas instâncias, transporte próprio, callbacks e framing foram
explicitadas de forma conservadora. A revisão final examinou ownership,
ponteiros, liberação parcial de lotes, limites de IDs, reinicialização,
composição de módulos e consistência entre código e documentação.

docs.title: Correções da auditoria LightnerX — registro histórico
docs.text:
Este documento preserva os resultados da auditoria de 12/11/2026, anterior à migração. O LightnerX atual usa C++17 e headers clássicos; a validação atual está em Migração C++17 e as instruções de build em Setup . Os caminhos da tabela abaixo foram atualizados para os arquivos atuais; os headers correspondentes estão em include/lightnerx/ . Números, logs e limitações descritos como históricos referem-se exclusivamente à auditoria.  Revisão de origem: 8e5a352 . Dependência GNS: d534c19 . Auditoria lida: LightnerX-audit.md . Trabalho validado em 12/11/2026 com GCC/libstdc++ 15.2,
CMake 4.2.3 e Ninja 1.13.2, em Linux.  Os 14 itens foram confrontados com a revisão de origem e receberam correções.
Naquela auditoria, C++26, módulos, GameNetworkingSockets, representação binária INER e queueMessage(OutboundMessage) com Target foram preservados. Não houve edição
de terceiros; a alteração preexistente em external/GameNetworkingSockets/examples/trivial_signaling_client.h foi mantida naquela auditoria.

docs.title: Resultado por item
docs.text:
Os nomes de testes abaixo são os sufixos dos testes CTest lightnerx.* .
Os caminhos de implementação sem prefixo estão em network/ .  LX Causa Correção implementada Arquivos de implementação/documentação Testes executados Classificação Pendências LX-01 Wrappers destruíam GNS diretamente, deixando flag e ponteiros inconsistentes. Encerramento central, ownership explícito, limpeza de membros e rollback de inicialização. network_manager.cpp , client.cpp , server.cpp , docs/api.md lifecycle , lifecycle_faults , integration Corrigido e validado Nenhuma funcional. LX-02 Consulta de identidade dependia de userdata em handle já fechado. Mapa reverso local mantém a identidade até remove() , inclusive nos callbacks após o fechamento. connection_manager.cpp , server.cpp , docs/api.md connection_manager , integration com desconexões pelos dois lados Corrigido e validado Nenhuma. LX-03 return false construía optional<uint16_t> presente com valor zero. Lookup ausente retorna nullopt ; zero não é um ID cadastrado. connection_manager.cpp connection_manager , messages Corrigido e validado Nenhuma. LX-04 Último ID não era reciclado; contador e índice de 16 bits transbordavam. Reciclagem de todos os IDs removidos, contador mais largo, domínio 1–65535 e iteração limitada com size_t . connection_manager.cpp , docs/api.md connection_manager : 70.000 ciclos; connection_manager_domain : domínio completo Corrigido e validado Domínio completo usa interface controlada, não 65.535 sockets reais simultâneos. LX-05 Cópia implícita duplicava ownership e ponteiros de callbacks. Cópia e movimentação excluídas em Client/Server; Server também encerra recursos no destrutor. client.cpp , server.cpp , docs/api.md lifecycle e consumer , com verificações de tipos em compilação Corrigido e validado Código consumidor que copiava wrappers deve ser adaptado. LX-06 Desconexão local não limpava handle e estado. Fechamento bem-sucedido invalida handle e limpa connected , permitindo reconexão. client.cpp , docs/api.md lifecycle_faults , integration Corrigido e validado Nenhuma. LX-07 Recebimento negativo era tratado como fila vazia. Retorna io_error ; cliente também fecha/limpa sua conexão inválida. client.cpp , server.cpp , docs/api.md lifecycle_faults , com retorno -1 nos dois caminhos Corrigido e validado Falha rara provocada por injeção controlada. LX-08 Cinco conversores desreferenciavam retorno nulo de AllocateMessage . Verificação comum lança bad_alloc ; tamanho irrepresentável lança length_error antes da alocação. communication/message.cpp , docs/api.md , docs/communication.md message_faults : cinco falhas de alocação e overflow; messages : GNS real Corrigido e validado Não foi necessário esgotar a memória do sistema. LX-09 C++26 e requisitos GNS não eram públicos no target; setup incompleto. cxx_std_26 e GNS públicos; configuração de import std e toolchain documentadas; consumidor independente. CMakeLists.txt , docs/setup.md , tests/consumer/ consumer , compilação completa CMake/Ninja Corrigido e validado Outras toolchains não foram homologadas. LX-10 Dois módulos exportavam constantes distintas com o mesmo nome. Uma declaração de k_invalidConnection no gerenciador global, reexportada por cliente e transporte. network_manager.cpp , client.cpp , transport.cpp consumer , lifecycle Corrigido e validado Nenhuma. LX-11 Instâncias competiam pelos callbacks e pela destruição global. Um wrapper iniciado por processo; conflitos e repetição de start são rejeitados; shutdown respeita o owner. network_manager.cpp , client.cpp , server.cpp , README.md , docs/api.md , docs/first-steps.md lifecycle , integration Corrigido e validado Coexistência de vários wrappers não faz parte do contrato suportado. LX-12 Userdata global permitia interferência entre managers e cadastros duplicados. Mapeamento bidirecional próprio, pertencimento local, rejeição de duplicatas e validação do handle GNS na admissão. connection_manager.cpp , README.md , docs/api.md connection_manager : duplicatas, managers independentes, userdata preservada Corrigido e validado Transporte externo não ganha suporte a IDs arbitrários; restrição documentada. LX-13 Parser ignorava divergência entre tamanho declarado e buffer. Exige uma mensagem completa, tamanho decodificado igual ao span e header mínimo completo. communication/message.cpp , docs/api.md , docs/communication.md messages , message_faults : truncamentos, concatenação, tamanhos inválidos e limites 15/16 bits Corrigido e validado Nenhuma mudança de framing ou formato binário. LX-14 Exceções vazavam buffers; registro reentrante invalidava vetores; forEach terminava o processo. RAII em recebimento e batching, callbacks em armazenamento estável, propagação de exceções, captura na fronteira GNS, bloqueio de update recursivo e fechamento adiado. client.cpp , server.cpp , connection_manager.cpp , network_manager.cpp , message_batch.cpp , communication/message.cpp , docs/api.md messages , message_faults , lifecycle_faults , connection_manager , integration ; ASan e UBSan conforme limites abaixo Corrigido, mas parcialmente validado UBSan modular indisponível no GCC 15.2; checagem vptr incompatível com GNS sem RTTI.

docs.title: Evidências e testes históricos
docs.text:
A suíte normal passou nos oito testes, sem testes ignorados. Resultados locais: build/audit/test-results.xml e build/audit/Testing/Temporary/LastTest.log .
A execução instrumentada final também passou nos oito testes, sem testes
ignorados e sem diagnósticos dos sanitizadores habilitados (53,47 segundos).
Resultados: build/audit-sanitizers/test-results.xml e build/audit-sanitizers/Testing/Temporary/LastTest.log . A suíte normal levou
131,90 segundos, incluindo a compilação do consumidor. Os limites abaixo são
parte da validação, não uma garantia de ausência de todos os defeitos possíveis.
A classificação final é de 13 itens corrigidos e validados e LX-14 corrigido,
mas parcialmente validado pelas restrições de instrumentação explicitadas.  Os executáveis connection_manager , messages e lifecycle importam os
  módulos reais e usam GNS real. Há testes de reinicialização, estados inválidos,
  identidade, serialização, ownership e callbacks. integration executa Client e Server em processos separados sobre UDP local.
  Testa três sessões, mensagens, reconexão, desconexão iniciada pelos dois lados,
  identidade após fechamento, exceção de admissão, registro reentrante de
  callbacks, update recursivo e encerramento/reinicialização do servidor. consumer configura um projeto pai independente, inclui headers Steam e
  importa módulos ligando somente o target LightnerX . Os três testes Python suplementares compilam corpos de produção sem as
  declarações de módulos. Interfaces controladas permitem esgotar os 65.535 IDs,
  devolver alocação nula e provocar erros de recebimento/liberação. Eles não
  substituem os testes dos módulos reais. Contadores verificam a liberação de
  mensagens, inclusive após uma parte do lote já ter sido processada.  Reproduções anteriores às correções incluíram: Client copiável; três mensagens
retidas após exceção; desconexão com connected=true ; erro de recebimento
reportado como sucesso; inicialização global verdadeira com interface nula;
start simultâneo/repetido aceito; optional inválido com valor zero; duplicatas;
overflow de IDs; tamanho INER inválido entregue; alocação nula causando falha.
O consumidor original não encontrava o header Steam e compilava em C++17.
O teste de domínio também foi aplicado ao arquivo original de 8e5a352 e falhou
em exhausted ID domain must reject add ( build/audit/id-baseline.log ).

docs.title: Reprodução com a versão C++17 atual
docs.text:
Os comandos abaixo executam a suíte atual; não recriam os oito testes históricos. Para reproduzir o ambiente antigo, use a revisão e a toolchain daquela auditoria. O problema UBSan/módulos descrito abaixo não se aplica mais à implementação C++17; somente a incompatibilidade de vptr com GNS sem RTTI permanece.  cmake -S . -B build/audit -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DLIGHTNERX_BUILD_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build/audit --parallel 2
ctest --test-dir build/audit --output-on-failure --output-junit test-results.xml -j 2

cmake -S . -B build/audit-sanitizers -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DLIGHTNERX_BUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DLIGHTNERX_SANITIZERS=address,undefined
cmake --build build/audit-sanitizers --parallel 2
ctest --test-dir build/audit-sanitizers --output-on-failure --output-junit test-results.xml -j 2  O teste UDP e LeakSanitizer precisam de permissões que o sandbox inicial não
oferecia. A execução final usa o ambiente autorizado fora dessa restrição.
O limite dos testes que compilam código foi ampliado para 180 segundos após um
timeout de compilação concorrente; os limites de runtime permanecem delimitados.

docs.title: Limites históricos dos sanitizadores
docs.text:
Os módulos LightnerX e os consumidores foram compilados com ASan. Os três testes
suplementares usam ASan e UBSan, com -fno-sanitize-recover=all , para que qualquer
diagnóstico habilitado resulte em falha. A biblioteca padrão e o GNS não foram
instrumentados nem tiveram seus fontes alterados.  GCC 15.2 aborta com erro interno cp/module.cc:10037 ao compilar estes módulos
com UBSan. Isso foi reproduzido tanto instrumentando std quanto deixando std sem instrumentação; portanto não se declara cobertura UBSan dos módulos reais.  O GNS vendorizado usa -fno-rtti . Uma reprodução independente, contendo apenas
Init/CreatePollGroup/DestroyPollGroup/Kill de GNS, já produz o diagnóstico vptr
do UBSan, sem usar LightnerX. O mesmo programa passa quando somente essa checagem
é desabilitada ( build/audit/gns-ubsan-probe.cpp e .log ). Por isso apenas o
teste suplementar de ciclo de vida, que chama a biblioteca real, usa -fno-sanitize=vptr . Os outros dois testes suplementares não precisam dessa
exclusão. Esse diagnóstico foi investigado mesmo quando CTest inicialmente
reportou sucesso por causa do modo recuperável padrão do UBSan.

docs.title: API pública e contratos preservados
docs.text:
Client e Server não podem mais ser copiados ou movidos. Server ganha destrutor
  com limpeza automática; close() é idempotente e noexcept . Apenas um Client ou Server iniciado possui a rede por processo. Start repetido
  retorna operation_in_progress ; outro owner retorna device_or_resource_busy . networkKill() não invalida um wrapper ativo; o encerramento ocorre quando o
  owner libera os recursos. Raw GNS Kill/RunCallbacks durante esse ownership não
  são operações suportadas. disconnect() limpa o estado local imediatamente. Erros de recebimento passam
  a retornar io_error . Callbacks podem lançar; buffers são liberados e a
  exceção é propagada. Não se deve destruir o objeto que está despachando um
  callback. forEach deixa de ser incondicionalmente noexcept . getClientId() consulta pertencimento ao manager e não userdata GNS. A
  identidade persiste até remoção explícita. O manager deixa userdata para a
  aplicação. Capacidades negativas são rejeitadas; o domínio é limitado a 65535. Conversores mantêm assinaturas e lançam bad_alloc / length_error em falhas.
  Mensagens recebidas com tamanho inconsistente são rejeitadas sem callback,
  conforme a interface de parsing existente, que retorna void . Adicionados clearMessagesBatcher() e Target::isGroup() . A API queueMessage() /Target permanece; mensagens pendentes são liberadas no
  encerramento e após exceções. initMessagesBatcher() não descarta a fila. Há uma única constante pública k_invalidConnection . CMake agora propaga C++17 e
  os requisitos públicos GNS. O consumidor inclui os headers clássicos descritos em Setup .  Não há decisão arquitetural pendente para as correções adotadas. As restrições
de múltiplas instâncias, transporte próprio, callbacks e framing foram
explicitadas de forma conservadora. A revisão final examinou ownership,
ponteiros, liberação parcial de lotes, limites de IDs, reinicialização,
composição de módulos e consistência entre código e documentação.
